solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Little image I doctored that's improper

indicators.note: a document that has been doctored has been tampered with, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has tampered with a small picture, and the speaker objects that this was not the proper thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctored' is the anagram signal applied to the twelve letters of 'Little image I'; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something improper is not according to the rules, which is the core sense of unlawful or not legitimate.

clue.text: Restrict interest about who is regularly meeting heads of British Intelligence

indicators.note: about means around, so INT goes around the other pieces

parts.note: INT is the abbreviation for interest

indicators.note: meeting says these pieces join up side by side
regularly picks every other letter of the words after it
the heads of words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Someone limits the interest of a person who often meets the chiefs of British intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: Every other letter of 'who is' gives HI.
explanation.definitionFit: To curb or hold back something is to restrict it.

clue.text: Large round bottom, hard to ignore in yoga position

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: to ignore means to leave out, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: tush is a slang word for the backside
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A well-rounded rear end must be disregarded when sitting in a yoga pose.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the cross-legged seated asana named after a flower.

clue.text: Chatty daughter gets posh replacement in organisation of Lord Sugar

indicators.note: organisation means arranging, so the letters are put in a new order
replacement means one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, so posh

explanation.surface: A talkative daughter lands a smart new job in Lord Sugar's company.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Sugar is the British businessman of TV's The Apprentice; replacing D with U gives LORUSUGAR, rearranged by 'organisation of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Garrulous means talking too much, an extreme form of chatty.

clue.text: President Donald's tense over son visiting this country

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so first

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: visiting means going into, so this letter sits inside

parts.note: for a British newspaper this country is the UK

explanation.surface: An American president named Donald is anxious about his son visiting Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President Donald' suggests Trump; it is Donald Tusk, President of the European Council (2014-19). The 's is a link (is).
explanation.definitionFit: The Polish politician Donald Tusk held the office of President of the European Council.

clue.text: Rubbish seen over heathland about to increase rapidly

parts.note: mush is nonsense or rubbish

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a moor is open heathland

explanation.surface: Rubbish has been seen piling up on moorland at a fast rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow quickly is to shoot up overnight like a fungus, the verb sense.

clue.text: Score for perfect dive secures satisfactory mark

indicators.note: secures means holds tight, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: ten is the top score a judge can award a dive
OK means satisfactory

explanation.surface: A diver's perfect score earns a respectable grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a sign or symbol, so a mark of something, as in a token of respect.

clue.text: Went and got married again?

definitions.meaning: to go to a place, as in withdrew to the drawing room

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person went off and wed for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the punning second reading, split as RE-PAIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Repair is a formal verb for going somewhere; re-paired means paired off anew, as by a wedding.

clue.text: Agree never to bring up somewhat superficial appearance

indicators.note: to bring up says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone vows never to raise a matter that is only skin-deep.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to bring up' means read upwards: REENEV from 'Agree never' read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin decorative surface layer covering something cheaper; figuratively a mere outward show.

clue.text: Hybrid vigour evenly distributed in sheep, they're of such impressive size originally

indicators.note: evenly picks the even-numbered letters, the second, fourth and so on, running through the two words that follow
originally points to the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A breeder notes that a cross between sheep spreads its benefits evenly, producing animals of remarkable size.
explanation.walkthrough: Even letters of 'sheep, they're' give HETER; the initials of 'of such impressive size' give OSIS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the geneticists' technical name for the extra vigour and size often shown by crossbred offspring.

clue.text: Articulate supporter of Hull University

indicators.note: to articulate is to say out loud, so the word for the supporter is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the keel is the main structural timber running along the bottom of a ship's hull, holding it up

explanation.surface: Someone well-spoken backs the University of Hull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hull University' looks like a single institution; Hull is a ship's hull. Keele University is in Staffordshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Keele is an English campus institution near Newcastle-under-Lyme, so it is one example of a place of higher learning.

clue.text: Question put in vulgar language

indicators.note: put in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: base means low, coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: A query is phrased in crude, rude words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vulgar language' reads as swearing, but 'language' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Basque is the tongue spoken in the western Pyrenees, unrelated to any other living European speech.

clue.text: Shorten lead of Newfoundland approaching pet right outside

indicators.note: outside says the word for right goes around the other pieces

parts.note: true means right or correct

indicators.note: approaching means coming up to, so one piece sits right before the next
the lead of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a cat is a common household pet

explanation.surface: Someone cuts short the lead of their Newfoundland dog as it nears a pet cat outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a dog lead, fitting the Newfoundland breed of dog; it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To truncate something is to cut off part of it, making it briefer.

clue.text: Stand with legs splayed out from port I'd drunk

indicators.note: a drunk is all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who drank too much port ended up sprawled with legs akimbo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera or surveyor's support rests on three legs set wide apart for stability.

clue.text: Break in play when vile rant is broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered, as seed, so the letters are spread about

explanation.surface: A pause in a theatre performance arrives when an abusive tirade goes out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In the theatre the pause between acts is the time audiences go to the bar.

clue.text: Learn panel member is someone capable of trickery

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
a juror is a member of a jury panel

explanation.surface: Finding out that someone sitting on a jury is a trickster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learn' looks like 'find out'; here it is the archaic CON, to study.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician performs sleight of hand, which is trickery for entertainment.

clue.text: Average chap, patient individual, fells timber we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: Job is the biblical figure famous for his patience, and to log is to fell trees for timber, so together they say Job logs

explanation.surface: An ordinary man patiently cuts down trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' looks like someone in hospital; it means long-suffering Job. The name is the British everyman, like John Doe.
explanation.definitionFit: The British name for a typical ordinary member of the public, a hypothetical everyman.

clue.text: On sale, 50% off, spot a fine sort of table

indicators.note: in a down clue on means sitting above, so the spot comes first

parts.note: a drop is a spot of liquid

indicators.note: half the word is taken off, leaving its latter half

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A shop advertises half-price goods, spotting a fine bargain in a type of table.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% off' leaves the last half of 'sale', LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A table with a hinged flap that folds down when not in use.

clue.text: One's enthralled by subject in school essay that shows creativity

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive by, so the first piece is held inside the others

parts.note: art is a school subject
an essay is an attempt, which is a try
one is I, and the 's is is, giving I and IS together as IS

explanation.surface: Someone is captivated by a school subject in an essay displaying flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' gives I plus 'S (is), the two letters IS. 'essay' is an attempt, not a school composition.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is skill and imagination in making things, which amounts to creativity.

clue.text: Attractive quality that a cricketer hopes is successful?

definitions.meaning: charm or allure that draws people

definitions.text: that a cricketer hopes is successful?
definitions.meaning: a fielder's shout to the umpire asking for a batsman to be given out

explanation.surface: A cricketer hopes charm will win the day.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, fielders shout 'Howzat?' to ask the umpire to give the batter out.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the noun: allure, and a formal request to the umpire.

clue.text: Rarely struts catwalk promoting line from the East

indicators.note: in an across clue, from the East means read from right to left
promoting means moving up, so the line letter is shifted earlier in the word

parts.note: a fashion model who struts the catwalk models clothes

explanation.surface: A fashion model seldom parades on the runway pushing a range of goods from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoting' moves L forward in MODELS to give MODLES; 'from the East' then reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom and rarely are synonyms, both meaning not often.

clue.text: In Paris, my uncle loses second new visual aid

indicators.note: loses second says the second of two such letters is dropped

parts.note: mon oncle is French for my uncle

explanation.surface: A French uncle mislays his new pair of glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: A single lens worn in one eye to help sight, so an aid to vision.

clue.text: Norm shreds vegetables

parts.note: par is the normal or standard level
snips are small cut pieces, shreds

explanation.surface: A man called Norm cuts up vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norm' looks like a man's name; it means par.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsnips are root crops eaten as vegetables.

clue.text: Name that is extremely crude to give a relative

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, the outer letters

explanation.surface: Calling a family member something very rude.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member.

clue.text: Inform university a German is joining about end of April

indicators.note: is joining says this piece attaches to those before it

parts.note: C is short for circa, meaning about

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: ein is the German for a

explanation.surface: Telling a university that a German student is enrolling around the end of April.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone in the picture is to give them the facts, an idiom for informing them.

clue.text: Run more than usual

definitions.meaning: in cricket a run scored not off the bat, such as a bye or wide

explanation.definitionFit: Cricket counts byes and wides as runs added to the total; the adjective means additional.

clue.text: Eyes Mark endlessly, before Gregory it was Julian!

indicators.note: endlessly means without both ends, leaving the inner letters of each word

explanation.surface: Mark is watched and told that before Gregory the man was Julian.
explanation.walkthrough: Pope Gregory XIII's calendar of 1582 replaced the Julian calendar of Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: The calendar measure of twelve months was reckoned by Julian rules until Gregorian reform.

clue.text: Shock of orchard essentially disappearing in morning mist

parts.note: AM is short for ante meridiem, the morning

indicators.note: disappearing in says the letter is removed from inside the next word

parts.note: haze is a mist

indicators.note: essentially means at its essence or core, the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: A picture of an orchard vanishing into the early morning fog.
explanation.walkthrough: The central letter of 'orchard' is H, removed from HAZE.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound or astonish someone is to give them a shock.

clue.text: Active English politician, gutless to block call for review

indicators.note: review is read as re-view, looking back, so the letters are reversed
to block means to get in the way, so this piece sits inside the next

parts.note: to cite is to call or summon, as a witness

indicators.note: gutless means with the insides removed, here the middle letter

parts.note: a Green is a member of an environmentalist party

explanation.surface: An energetic English MP who lacks courage tries to stop a demand for an inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' removes the central letter of the Green, leaving GREN after E; 'to block' sets that inside CITE, and 'for review' (re-view, looking back) turns CITEGRENE round.
explanation.definitionFit: An energetic person is lively and busy, which is being active.

clue.text: Unfortunately we fear latest governmental social benefit system

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: We dread the newest piece of government welfare policy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a national scheme of state-funded pensions, healthcare and payments to the needy.
